found_by: adversarial review (role-a-review workflow, 3 Oct 2026), each finding confirmed by a second agent
protocol: the frozen set is not changed; report XA on all items and on all items except those listed here (selrm.xr.crossed_accuracy(..., exclude=...))

issues.reason: Inclusivity items on age: the contested case states the age exactly at the threshold ('aged 65 years'). Age in years is read as completed years, so a patient aged 65 is between 65.0 and 66; a literal reader can hold that 'more than 65 years' is true, which flips the exclusive rule's label.

Currency items on diabetes: the contested case is diabetes in remission, which the program treats as not current. Remission is not cure (ADA/EASD 2021 consensus; ICD-10-CM codes type 2 diabetes in remission as a diabetes diagnosis), so a careful reader can hold that the patient currently has diabetes, which flips the 'currently has' rule's label.

design_notes.reason: In the window dimension the date form is confounded with the clause phrasing: phrasing 1 items always use month-and-year dates, phrasings 0 and 2 always use 'N months ago'. Do not report window results by phrasing or by date form.

Age-inclusivity items take the patient's age from the threshold, not from the scenario's age range, so some cases are implausible for their scenario (e.g. a request for contraception at 57 or older). Labels are unaffected.

A DVT template says the clot was 'diagnosed ... and completed treatment'; at under three months before the visit this is clinically implausible (treatment lasts at least three months). Labels are unaffected.

The hip-osteoarthritis scenario chooses between naproxen alone and naproxen with omeprazole, which only gastrointestinal risk plausibly affects; the fit table pairs it with other conditions by word match. Labels are unaffected.

The conclusion claims are the scenario's two options and differ in length by up to 2 words (rule_v1's constraint rules: at most 2). Scorers that use claim likelihood should compare within an item, which XA does.
The stored prose field quotes the full rule clause as the condition, which reads awkwardly; do not use xr_v1's prose as a program-supplied summary.

MANIFEST git_commit (6966837) predates the commit that added the generator (2df9308, selrm/xr.py and scripts/build_xr_v1.py). The records regenerate byte-identically from the current code: python scripts/build_xr_v1.py --restore checks the frozen sha256.

The generator keeps at least two months between an event and the start of the window (W months before the visit). Positive events are 1 to W-2 months before the visit, so for a 3-month window they are exactly 1 month before it. The month-level date can never reach the visit date, so labels are unaffected; the MANIFEST's 'every window edge' overstates this.
